capitals.name: Indraprastha (Indapatta, near Delhi)
capitals.note: 'According to the Jatakas, the capital of the Kurus was Indraprastha (Indapatta) near modern Delhi'; the Kuru page's infobox lists Āsandīvat, Hastinapura and Indraprastha and says the capital 'was later transferred to Kaushambi, in the lower Doab' after Hastinapur's floods (Vedic, before this window).

correction.text: 'The country of the Kurus roughly corresponded to the modern Thanesar, state of Delhi, and Meerut district of Uttar Pradesh' (Mahajanapadas page); 'The area formerly occupied by the Kuru Kingdom covered the presently Thanesar, Delhi, and most of the upper Gangetic Doab' (Kuru page); capital Indraprastha (Indapatta) near modern Delhi; drawn as one country: Delhi and Cliopatria's disc, with circles at Ghaziabad, Meerut, Sonipat and Panipat and one at Karnal standing for Thanesar (33 km away) until the gazetteer has it

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 5,232 km2 disc is centred on Delhi (77.28E 28.65N). The Mahajanapadas page has the Kuru country 'roughly corresponded to the modern Thanesar, state of Delhi, and Meerut district of Uttar Pradesh'; the Kuru page gives 'Thanesar, Delhi, and most of the upper Gangetic Doab' for the old Vedic kingdom (c. 1200-900 BCE), which by the Buddha's time 'had become a minor state ruled by a chieftain called Koravya', so the Mahajanapada wording is used. Neither page has an area. The first version (Delhi, a 40 km circle at Meerut and one at Thanesar, about 10,500 km2) resolved to three separate islands (5, 19 and 18 cells; Thanesar is not in the gazetteer), leaving Ghaziabad and the Sonipat-Panipat-Karnal country unowned and dropping Cliopatria's disc around Delhi, although the pages describe one country ('stretching from the Gaṅgā and the border of the Pañcāla in the east to the Sarasvatī', Kuru page). Corrected after the adversarial review of 2026-10-18: Cliopatria's disc, Delhi, and circles at Ghaziabad (25 km), Meerut (35 km), Sonipat (30 km), Panipat (30 km) and Karnal (40 km, standing for Thanesar, 33 km away, which the gazetteer lacks): 59 cells, about 15,600 km2 (3.0 times the disc), one piece, holding all 18 cells of Cliopatria's disc, Indraprastha and the Thanesar cell. The radii are my reading; the circles at Ghaziabad, Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal are the country between the three places the page names, and shrink or grow with that reading. Kuru 'switched to a republican form of government during the 6th to 5th centuries BCE' (Mahajanapadas); the land is unchanged.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -404..-346: Cliopatria ends the Kuru in -405, the year before its Shaishunaga row starts, but the Kuru page's infobox runs 'c. 1900 BCE - c. 345 BCE' and the Mahajanapadas page has the Kurus attested 'in the 4th century BCE' by Kautilya's Arthashastra. No page opened says the Shaishunaga took the Kuru; the shape is the corrected -600 land carried to c. 345. This does not collide with Cliopatria's Shaishunaga row (-404..-334, 797,305 km2): its bounding box reaches only 27.67N while the Kuru country lies at 28.3-30.0N, and the gazetteer finds 0 cells shared between that row and the Kuru land. The Kuru page was reopened in the repair: it does not say who ended the kingdom or when (no Nandas, nothing at c. 345 BCE), so the end stays the infobox's.

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: the Kuru, a janapada around Indraprastha, stand as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas. 'The Kuru Kingdom was formed in the Middle Vedic period (c. 1200 - c. 900 BCE)' and had become 'something of a backwater' by the Mahajanapada period; -600 is Cliopatria's start of the Mahajanapadas, so the year is a bridge and the Vedic life is not drawn.

ledger.note: c. 345 BCE: the Kuru state ends. The page's infobox runs 'c. 1900 BCE - c. 345 BCE' and 'Disestablished' carries no explanation; the Mahajanapadas page has the Kurus still attested 'in the 4th century BCE' by the Arthashastra and 'The Nandas usurped the throne of Shishunaga dynasty c. 345 BCE' in the same year, but no page ties the Kuru to the Nandas. Cliopatria ends the row in -405. Who took the land is not said. Reopened in the repair of 2026-10-18: the Kuru page never says who ended the kingdom and does not mention the Nandas or c. 345 BCE; its only statement of decline is 'The Kurus declined after being defeated by the non-Vedic Salva (or Salvi) tribe' (Vedic period).

certainty.note: Only the Ganga and Yamuna doab and the Sarasvati/Drishadvati country around Kurukshetra are named; the Panchala and Matsya frontiers are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's Kuru (-600..-405, two identical 5,232 km2 discs on Delhi) is widened to one contiguous country from Delhi and Meerut to the Karnal-Thanesar country (the Mahajanapadas page; 59 cells, about 15,600 km2) and extended to c. 345 BCE (the Kuru page's infobox end; Mahajanapadas: Kurus attested in the 4th century by the Arthashastra), with a new keyframe -404..-346; the end is the page's, not Cliopatria's. Cliopatria's Shaishunaga row (-404..-334, 797,305 km2) does not collide with the Kuru land (its bbox reaches only 27.67N, the Kuru country lies at 28.3-30.0N, 0 cells shared; the first version of these notes said it covered this country, which was wrong): no page opened has the Shaishunaga conquer the Kuru (the Shishunaga pages cited by the Avanti dossier name Avanti, Kosala and Vatsa). Left out for want of a dated page: the Kuru dynasty 'evolved into Kuru and Vatsa Kingdom' by the 6th century BCE (Kuru page; the Vatsa row exists from -600), the earlier Salva defeat and floods at Hastinapur (Vedic), the small Kuru states of Indapatta and Iṣukāra. No ruler list is documented in the pages (a chieftain 'Koravya'). No wars in the window. Pages: Kuru Kingdom and the shared Mahajanapadas page. Gazetteer lacks: Thanesar (place, 29.97N 76.83E, Kurukshetra), no longer used in a region (Karnal 40 km stands for it), also Kurukshetra and Hastinapur. Repair of 2026-10-18 (after the adversarial review): the first union (Delhi, Meerut 40 km, Thanesar 40 km) was three islands and dropped Cliopatria's disc; it is now one piece (Cliopatria's disc, Delhi, Ghaziabad 25 km, Meerut 35 km, Sonipat 30 km, Panipat 30 km, Karnal 40 km for Thanesar) in all three keyframes and both events, 59 cells, about 15,600 km2. The Mahajanapadas and Kuru pages were reopened for the extent sentences; neither names Ghaziabad, Sonipat, Panipat or Karnal, so those radii are my reading of 'one country' between the three places named.
